title: cgroup v2: controllers, CPU throttling and memory limits
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: In cgroup v2 there is one tree under /sys/fs/cgroup.
cpu.weight is a relative share used when the CPU is busy, which maps to a CPU request.
A multi threaded service with a limit of one CPU can burn its quota in a few milliseconds across many threads, and then freeze for the rest of the period.
memory.max is a hard limit. This keeps the next step safe and easy to check.
memory.events counts how many times the group hit high, max and oom_kill.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: Slow responses with idle CPUs
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
Latency doubled in one service while node CPU showed forty percent idle.
An operator runs a command such as: cat /sys/fs/cgroup/kubepods.slice/kubepods-burstable.slice/cpu.stat
The service had a CPU limit of one core but ran sixteen threads, so it used its quota in the first few milliseconds of many periods and then stopped.
More than seventy percent of periods were throttled.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Reading node CPU only and not cgroup throttling.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: The CPU scheduler, run queues, NUMA and pinning
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: Each CPU has a queue of runnable tasks.
Normal tasks use the fair scheduler, which shares CPU by weight, and nice values change the weight.
Network cards and disks raise interrupts that are handled on some cores.
On a multi socket server, each socket has local memory, and access to the other socket is slower.
Pinning a process to specific cores, or isolating cores from the general scheduler, reduces jitter for latency critical work such as packet processing.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: One busy core, fifteen idle
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
Network throughput stopped growing on a fast server although total CPU use was low.
An operator runs a command such as: mpstat -P ALL 1 1 | sort -k12 -n | head -3
All interrupts for the network card were handled by core zero, which spent nearly all its time in softirq while other cores idled.
The packet rate was limited by that single core.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Reading load average as CPU use only.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: Virtual memory: page tables, huge pages, swap and pressure
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: Each process sees its own virtual address space.
Spare memory is used for the page cache, which holds file data.
Normal pages are 4 kilobytes. This keeps the next step safe and easy to check.
Swap lets the kernel move rarely used anonymous pages out, which frees memory for cache.
Pressure stall information reports the share of time tasks stalled waiting for memory.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: The database that stalled every few minutes
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
Query latency spiked for a few seconds at regular intervals on a database host with plenty of free memory.
An operator runs a command such as: cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled
Transparent huge pages were set to always, and the kernel stalled the database while it compacted memory to build huge pages.
The stall counters matched the latency spikes.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Alerting on free memory instead of pressure.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: The block layer: NVMe queues, schedulers and io_uring
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: A normal write goes into the page cache and returns quickly.
An fsync call asks for the data to reach stable storage and waits for the device to confirm.
The block layer turns file system requests into device requests, merges adjacent ones and orders them.
NVMe devices have many hardware queues, and Linux maps them to CPUs so that submission does not take a shared lock.
io_uring gives applications a pair of shared ring buffers to submit many IO requests and collect results with few system calls.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: Commits that took a second
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
A database showed slow commits while the average disk utilisation looked low.
An operator runs a command such as: iostat -x 1 2 | tail -4

The average utilisation looked acceptable, but the await value of thirty eight milliseconds and a queue of thirty six requests showed that writes waited behind a large background job that wrote at full speed.
The team limited the job with the io controller, moved its output to another device and set an alert on await and queue depth.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Judging a disk by utilisation alone.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: Container runtime internals: runc, overlayfs, seccomp and capabilities
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: A container runtime such as containerd prepares an image and a bundle, then runc creates new namespaces for the process: process IDs, mounts, network, hostname, inter process communication and sometimes users.
An overlay mounts several read only image layers under one writable layer.
Linux splits the powers of root into capabilities such as binding low ports, changing file ownership or loading modules.
A seccomp profile is a filter that allows, denies or logs system calls by number and arguments.
When something is denied, check in order: file permissions and user, capabilities, seccomp, then mandatory access control such as AppArmor or SELinux, then mounts and read only settings.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: The write that was blocked by a filter
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
A monitoring agent in a container failed with operation not permitted although it ran as root.
An operator runs a command such as: grep -E "CapEff|Seccomp" /proc/self/status
The agent called a system call to read performance counters, which the default seccomp profile does not allow, and root in a container does not add the missing capability.
The security team approved a narrow custom profile for that one system call and the capability it needed, applied only to that agent.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Running containers as privileged.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: The network stack path: netfilter, TCP buffers and XDP
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: A packet arrives at the network card, which writes it to a receive ring in memory and raises an interrupt.
Netfilter provides hooks where rules can accept, drop or change packets, and nftables is the current rule language.
Each socket has send and receive buffers.
The congestion algorithm decides how fast a sender grows and shrinks its rate.
XDP runs a small verified program at the earliest point in the driver, before the full stack allocates buffers.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: New connections dropped at random
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
A proxy host dropped about one in twenty new connections during peak traffic.
An operator runs a command such as: dmesg | grep -i conntrack | tail -2
The connection tracking table was full, because the proxy opened many short outbound connections and kept entries for a long timeout.
The kernel dropped packets for new flows.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Ignoring conntrack table usage.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.
